items.note: Vector art, not a bitmap: 3,950 drawing paths inside a 288.0 by 288.0 pt box whose only frame is a hairline rectangle at 155.4 to 440.7 pt square, with no axes, no ticks, no gridlines, no legend and no title inside the frame. Nodes print as small red triangles and edges as thin blue straight segments with arrowheads, so the drawing is directed even though the co-author relation it depicts is symmetric. No node carries a label or an id and no edge carries a weight, so nothing in the art can be counted at 150 dpi: the dense middle is an unresolved mat of blue lines and a few dozen isolated red triangles sit outside it, which is the 2-D stress-majorisation layout the surrounding prose blames for 'the unclear large-degree vertices'. The caption prints 20 pt under the foot rule at y 421.0 and is cut cleanly from the layer. Four by-number cita-tions, three of them on p5 a page before the art and the fourth on p10.

items.note: Wide vector drawing, 428.6 by 139.4 pt, 132 drawing paths and 92 curves, with no frame, axis, tick, legend or title inside it. Sixteen nodes print as square-cornered rectangles on a pale yellow fill (1.000/1.000/0.698) with a blue-violet border (0.298/0.298/1.000) at 0.425 pt, holding black ArialMT text at 3.98 pt in the label form 'AuthorYear(Cite:n)': Snijders2011(33), Watts2007(680), Watts2002(835), Kleinberg2000(1246), Barabasi1999(18843), Watts1998(21688), Albert2002(13250), Newman2001(2)(2748), Newman2003(10616), Newman2001(1523), Valente1996(498), Borgatti2000(763), Bonacich1987(1956), Bollobas2001(5957), Erdos1959(4531) and Ahuja1993(9153). The labels are 150-dpi illegible one character at a time - the first pass misread nine of the sixteen citation counts - and were transcribed from a 600 dpi render of the same page, against which the text layer agrees on all sixteen strings. Thirty-two filled triangular arrowheads on gray strokes (0.496/0.496/0.496) at 0.212 pt, so every connector is directed; 28 of the 60 connector fragments carry cubic Bezier segments, so roughly half the edges arc. No label overlaps another label or any stroke, and the arrowheads touch box borders without covering glyphs. The text layer offers 'Matlab 2011a' as a caption above the region, which is the toolbox credit mid-paragraph, not a caption; the real caption prints under the drawing. Three by-number citations: two on p10 itself and one on p11 reading it as evidence that Table 8's papers are cited while Table 9's cite.

note:
Fifteen measured regions over ten of twenty pages, all accounted for: fifteen rows - two figures and thirteen tables - no exclusions, no refusals, nothing unmeasured. The paper numbers nineteen tables and two figures, so six of the twenty-one printed exhibits have no region and are declared gaps rather than invented boxes: Table 3 on p6, Table 4 on p7, Table 5 on p8, Table 6 on p9, Table 18 on p17 and Table 19 on p18. All six are real booktabs grids - the drawing pass finds three ruled lines each, at 464.9, 482.0 and 618.7 pt on p6, at 260.8, 277.9 and 402.6 pt on p7, at 140.2, 157.4 and 282.1 pt on p8, at 218.8, 235.9 and 360.6 pt on p9, at 140.2, 157.4 and 282.1 pt on p17 and at 137.6, 154.7 and 195.7 pt on p18 - and every one of them is lost to the same half-page threshold as paper 67's three ghosts: their rules span 233.2, 244.8, 233.2, 252.7, 292.1 and 193.5 pt, which is 39.2, 41.1, 39.2, 42.4, 49.1 and 32.5 per cent of the 595.3 pt page width, against the 297.64 pt the detector requires. Table 18 misses by 5.5 pt, the closest call this lane has recorded. Their contents are on the record here anyway, read off the rendered pages: Tables 3, 4, 5 and 6 all print eleven rows over three columns - Rank, Name, Centrality - listing the ten researchers with the largest degree, eigenvector, closeness and betweenness centrality, the same ten names in four different orders; Table 18 prints the same eleven rows for the best co-author to add by closeness centrality, 0.020193 down to 0.020145, one page after Table 17 gives the eigenvector answer for the same question; and Table 19 prints four rows over five columns, 'Largest Deviation' plus DC, EC, CC and BC, with the three rows 0, 1, 2 and the counts 4, 8, 7, 3 / 3, 1, 3, 5 / 3, 1, 0, 2.

One ruling register, nineteen times over. Every grid in the paper is three horizontal rules over one header band and a body, with no vertical rule anywhere, and every grid is centred on the page axis rather than set flush - which is why the widths run from 72.6 to 100.1 per cent of the measure and why the six ghosts above were narrow enough to disappear. The counted widths in order of printing: 84.0, 87.2, 93.7, 92.7, 100.1, 86.7, 82.4, 76.5, 82.4, 76.0, 76.5, 95.2 and 72.6 per cent.

Defects recorded, not corrected. Tables 15 and 16 print one identical caption, 'Top-5 Movie Actors in 2011-2013 Using Bipartite Graph Model', although Table 16's rows are films rather than actors and its DC column is missing altogether - the paper's own footnote 8 on p14 knows about the missing column and not about the caption. Table 2's prose reads 16 per cent of researchers off bins that give 88 of 511, which is 17.2 per cent. Table 7's caption and the paragraph above it claim the four measures 'give the same top influential researcher', which holds for rank 1 and fails immediately below it: SOS, VERA TURAN is 8th on DC, 19th on EC, 5th on CC and 3rd on BC, and the grid prints that row. Figure 2 draws sixteen papers, each labelled with its citation count, while the three grids built on the same citation network rank three papers per measure, and its labels are unreadable at 150 dpi - nine of the sixteen citation counts misread on the first pass - so they were transcribed from a 600 dpi render. Figure 1 draws directed arrowheads on a symmetric co-author relation. The detector's heading pass mistakes every rank column for a heading number, which is why the context dump carries '4 RODL, VOJTECH 43' and '6 TUZA, ZSOLT 40' as sections of the paper. The prose typos stand as printed: 'we count the degree of each vertices', 'The ranking of top singers as well as songwriters are given', and the footnote marker that collides with the full stop in 'Table 8 and Table 96 .'.
rules: rows counts every printed row including the header band, never the number of bands between rules: every counted grid in this paper prints one header band and its body, so Table 17's ten ranked researchers and its header are eleven rows over three rules [table.rows]

every printed grid in this paper is booktabs: nineteen tables, three horizontal rules each, and not one vertical stroke in twenty pages, so rule_style is booktabs and zebra is false throughout [table.rule_style]

a grid over 75 per cent of the local measure is full: twelve of the thirteen counted grids run 76.0 to 100.1 per cent of the 418.3 pt measure and Table 17 is the single exception at 72.6 per cent, recorded half, with each percentage named in its note [table.width]

a column of equal-width values is not decimal alignment: the centrality columns of Tables 11 to 17 and the rank columns everywhere are set on one width and centred or right-aligned, so nothing is aligned on a point and decimal_aligned is false in every grid [table.decimal_aligned]

a missing measure column is a column the grid does not print: Table 16 headers Rank, EC, CC and BC and records cols 4, because footnote 8 explains that degree centrality ranks nothing when every film has three actors [table.cols]

a header cell that holds running text is one printed cell: Table 10's MKC column is headed 'MKC(p = 1/2, b = 0.2)' and the text layer scatters it into three fragments, so the crop is authoritative for the header string [table.header_rows]

a note_sentence must be a printed sentence on the grid's own page or the next one, and a grid named only one page early keeps the field empty: Table 8's naming sentence prints on p10 and Tables 12 and 15 are named on p13 and p14 respectively, so all three leave note_sentence empty and the pointer goes into the item note [table.note_sentence]

two grids that print one identical caption are recorded as printed: Table 15 and Table 16 carry the same caption word for word, and the column number is the only difference on the page [caption.verbatim]

a caption line in the text layer is not a citation: Table 1 prints its number in its own caption and nowhere else, so count 0 with first_page null, exactly as Table 5 which is named only in its caption on p8 [mention.count]

a citation that lands a page before the grid records lead_pages 1 and one on the same page records 0: Tables 3, 8, 9, 12, 15, 16 and 18 are all named a page early, Figure 1 three times on p5 [mention.lead_pages]

a drawing of markers joined by lines is node-link-network and not flowchart-or-schematic whether the art is a vector graph or a toolbox screenshot, so Figure 1's 3,950 vector paths and Figure 2's 132 paths and 92 curves share one family [geometry.family]

printed_numbers records numerals the art carries of its own and data_labels records names set inside it: Figure 1 prints neither, Figure 2 prints both, since every node is a rounded rectangle holding 'AuthorYear(Cite:n)' [geometry.printed_numbers]
